For example, suppose account A (cold write) transfers Ether to account B (cold write), updating both A and B. Later in the same transaction, A (warm write) transfers Ether to account C (cold write). Would both operations still incur the same `ACCOUNT_WRITE` cost, regardless of the warm/cold status of the individual account writes? > So, is it correct to say that the similarity in the values I observed is merely coincidental? Would say yes, for example all tx sig recoveries are done in parallel, so cost is a lot lower, and it is hard to measure. Optimizing gas usage is effectively a legitimate way to increase block throughput, so the benefits are far from negligible. btw <@1361003005691822160> what team are you on? I'm just an individual developer who wants to contribute to building EIPs 🙏 > I also wanted to clarify the semantics of ACCOUNT_WRITE. Is it intended to represent the cost of updating both the caller and the callee as a single unit? I replied to this already, <@1361003005691822160>. `ACCOUNT_WRITE` is a single account write. The callee cost is part of `TX_BASE_COST` I'm not sure I understand. You describe `ACCOUNT_WRITE` as "a single account write", but operations that modify account state, such as `CALL` and `CREATE`, always result in two accounts being updated simultaneously. Am I misunderstanding something here? `ACCOUNT_WRITE` only covers the cost for the callee. If you see how we benchmarked `TX_BASE_COST` and how we justify what parts of the costs are considered there, you see that it includes the access and write for the caller. I've agreed from the beginning that `TX_BASE_COST` only accounts for the caller's cost. I was simply trying to understand how that value was derived, and I think I understand it now. That said, I'm still not entirely convinced by the explanation of `ACCOUNT_WRITE`. If this cost is intended to account only for the callee, is the cost of updating the caller—which occurs at the same time—implicitly folded into it? I don't find that interpretation particularly intuitive. The reason to have it separate is because there are eth transfers that don't require an update to the callee, e.g., a self-transfer or a transfer without value. So, we benchmark these cases seperately. That said, I don't think the fee structure should be skewed to accommodate a few exceptional cases. Those cases can still be handled without introducing an asymmetric fee model, can't they? that is the whole point of 2780 - instead of having all eth transfers cost the same 21k (which is too cheap in some cases and too expensive in others), we breakdown the cost of eth transfers based on their actual perf

excerpts.author: gaxanh
excerpts.content:
So, is it correct to say that the similarity in the values I observed is merely coincidental?

I also wanted to clarify the semantics of `ACCOUNT_WRITE`. Is it intended to represent the cost of updating both the caller and the callee as a single unit? If so, does that imply that the cost of account state transitions is identical across all execution paths?

For example, suppose account A (cold write) transfers Ether to account B (cold write), updating both A and B. Later in the same transaction, A (warm write) transfers Ether to account C (cold write). Would both operations still incur the same `ACCOUNT_WRITE` cost, regardless of the warm/cold status of the individual account writes?

excerpts.author: draganrakita
excerpts.content:
> So, is it correct to say that the similarity in the values I observed is merely coincidental?
Would say yes, for example all tx sig recoveries are done in parallel, so cost is a lot lower, and it is hard to measure. TX_BASE is good guess done in benchmark.

excerpts.author: draganrakita
excerpts.content:
> I also wanted to clarify the semantics of ACCOUNT_WRITE. Is it intended to represent the cost of updating both the caller and the callee as a single unit? If so, does that imply that the cost of account state transitions is identical across all execution paths?
This is not taken into account when doing calculations, we dont check if target has already changed or not. This is something that got proposed in saparate EIP but was not included in Glamsterdam.
